meta.title: Security — Evento
meta.description: How Evento secures accounts, the self-custodial wallet, payments, events, and data — and how to report a vulnerability.

header.title: How Evento protects you
header.subtitle: How we secure your account, wallet, events, and data, and how to report a vulnerability.

signIn.title: Passwordless sign-in
signIn.description: One-time email codes or Google, handled by Supabase Auth.

selfCustody.title: Self-custodial wallet
selfCustody.description: Your recovery phrase is created on your device. Evento never receives it.

seedEncryption.title: AES-256 seed encryption
seedEncryption.description: Locked with your PIN via PBKDF2-SHA256 at 1,000,000 iterations.

eventPasswords.title: Hashed event passwords
eventPasswords.description: Stored as salted scrypt hashes and checked in constant time.

transport.title: HTTPS everywhere
transport.description: HSTS, a Content Security Policy, and framing blocked on every page.

publicApi.title: Read-only public API
publicApi.description: Unkey-issued keys, 1,000 requests per day, public events only.

accounts.title: Accounts & sign-in
accounts.summary: No account passwords to leak or reuse.

wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.summary: Self-custodial Lightning wallet built on the Breez SDK (Spark).

payments.title: Payments
payments.summary: Bitcoin over Lightning, sent from your own wallet.

events.title: Events & privacy
events.summary: Hosts decide who sees what, and the API enforces it.

data.title: Your data
data.summary: Stored with Supabase, encrypted in transit.

platform.title: Platform protections
platform.summary: Defenses built into the app and the API.

developers.title: Developers & API keys
developers.summary: Scoped, revocable keys for read-only access.

disclosure.title: Report a vulnerability
disclosure.summary: Found a security issue? Tell us privately.

emailOrGoogle.title: Email codes or Google
emailOrGoogle.body: Sign in with a one-time code sent to your email, or with your Google account. Both run through Supabase Auth.

cookieSessions.title: Cookie sessions
cookieSessions.body: Your session is kept in cookies set by Supabase Auth and refreshed on each request.

serverVerified.title: Verified on the server
serverVerified.body: Signed-in API requests are re-validated with Supabase Auth on the server, using your session cookie or a Bearer token.

compromisedAccount.title: Compromised account
compromisedAccount.body: If you think someone else has access, email {email} right away.

keysOnDevice.title: Keys created on your device
keysOnDevice.body: Your 12-word BIP39 recovery phrase is generated in your browser. It is never sent to Evento’s servers.

encryptedAtRest.title: Encrypted at rest
encryptedAtRest.body: The phrase is encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a key derived from your 6-digit PIN (PBKDF2-SHA256, 1,000,000 iterations, random salt) through the browser’s Web Crypto API, then saved in this browser’s local storage.

shortLivedMemory.title: Short-lived in memory
shortLivedMemory.body: After you unlock, the decrypted phrase stays only in memory and is cleared when you lock the wallet or after 30 minutes.

backupsStayWithYou.title: Backups stay with you
backupsStayWithYou.body: Export a PIN-encrypted backup file, or reveal your recovery phrase after re-entering your PIN. Evento stores neither.

whatEventoCantDo.title: What Evento can’t do
whatEventoCantDo.body: We can’t see your phrase, reset your PIN, or restore your wallet. Lose your device and your backup, and the funds can’t be recovered.

lightningAddress.title: Lightning address
lightningAddress.body: Your @evento.cash address is registered through Breez and saved to your public profile so people can pay you.

signedNotices.title: Signed payment notices
signedNotices.body: When your address receives a payment, Breez sends Evento an HMAC-SHA256-signed webhook so we can email you. We keep the payment hash, amount, and sender comment.

ticketsPayHost.title: Tickets pay the host directly
ticketsPayHost.body: Ticket invoices come from the host’s Lightning address. Evento checks the invoice amount matches the order and confirms payment by matching the preimage to the payment hash.

orderStorage.title: What we store for orders
orderStorage.body: Payment hash, verification URL, and preimage as proof of payment. Invoices expire after 10 minutes.

privateByDefault.title: Private by default
privateByDefault.body: New events are private unless you make them public. Private events only reach people with the link and stay out of other people’s feeds.

passwordProtected.title: Password-protected events
passwordProtected.body: Event passwords are hashed with scrypt and a random 16-byte salt, then checked in constant time. Location, description, and payment handles stay hidden until the right password is entered.

signedAccessCookie.title: Signed access cookie
signedAccessCookie.body: A correct password sets an HttpOnly, HMAC-signed cookie scoped to that one event for 7 days. Hosts and confirmed guests don’t need it.

hiddenUntilApproved.title: Hidden until approved
hiddenUntilApproved.body: Registration events hide the location and guest list from unapproved guests by default. Hosts can hide the description too.

guestList.title: Guest list
guestList.body: Hosts can hide the guest list from everyone.

whereItLives.title: Where it lives
whereItLives.body: Account, profile, and event data are stored in Supabase and accessed through the Evento API.

encryptedInTransit.title: Encrypted in transit
encryptedInTransit.body: All traffic uses HTTPS. HSTS tells browsers to always use HTTPS for two years, subdomains included, and insecure requests are upgraded.

whatWeCollect.title: What we collect
whatWeCollect.body: The profile details you give us, your event activity, and device and usage data.

yourRights.title: Your rights
yourRights.body: Ask for access, correction, or deletion at privacy@evento.so.

rateLimits.title: Rate limits
rateLimits.body: Abuse-prone endpoints are throttled, for example invite emails (20 a day per user), AI descriptions (10 a minute), and discount-code checks (30 a minute per IP).

sanitizedRichText.title: Sanitized rich text
sanitizedRichText.body: Event descriptions, blog posts, and email blasts pass through DOMPurify with a strict tag and attribute allowlist. Links that open a new tab get rel="noopener noreferrer".

securityHeaders.title: Security headers
securityHeaders.body: A Content Security Policy allowlists scripts, frames, and network connections. Other sites can’t frame Evento, and nosniff, a strict referrer policy, and a Permissions-Policy (microphone off) apply to every page.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.body: The web client is open source under GPL-3.0, so anyone can audit it.

readOnlyApi.title: Read-only Public API
readOnlyApi.body: Only GET endpoints, returning published public events, their guest lists, and user event lists.

unkeyKeys.title: Unkey-issued keys
unkeyKeys.body: Keys carry only the events:read permission and go in the x-evento-api-key header.

shownOnce.title: Shown once, revocable
shownOnce.body: A key is shown once when created. Evento stores only Unkey’s key ID, and you can revoke keys any time (up to 10 per account).

apiRateLimited.title: Rate limited
apiRateLimited.body: 1,000 requests per day per key. Requests over the limit get HTTP 429.

embedApi.title: Embed API
embedApi.body: Needs no key and only returns published public events.

howToReport.title: How to report
howToReport.body: Email {email} with “Security report” in the subject. If you’re signed in, you can also use Help & Support. Please don’t open public GitHub issues for vulnerabilities.

whatToInclude.title: What to include
whatToInclude.body: The affected URL or endpoint, steps to reproduce, the impact you observed, and how to reach you.

inScope.title: In scope
inScope.body: The Evento web app, the Evento API, and the open-source web client.

outOfScope.title: Out of scope
outOfScope.body: Third-party services (Supabase, Breez, Google, Unkey), denial-of-service or volume testing, spam, social engineering, and attacks that need an already-compromised device.

groundRules.title: Ground rules
groundRules.body: Use your own accounts and test data, don’t access other people’s data, and give us reasonable time to fix the issue before you disclose it.
